# GitHub Repositories

Fetches information regarding the repository, including

- Repository metadata and settings
- Configured workflows
- Recent workflow runs
- Optional direct Go dependency health and supply-chain visibility facts

This plugin is intended to be run as part of an aggregate agent, and will execute the policy suite for each repository.

This page is for **operators** who run the `plugin-github-repositories` plugin with the CCF Agent, and for **developers** who write policies for it. It documents [v0.12.0](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-github-repositories/releases/tag/v0.12.0) and is generated from the plugin's [README at v0.12.0](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-github-repositories/blob/v0.12.0/README.md).

## Requirements

### Authentication

The plugin authenticates with a token (a fine-grained personal access token, for example) or as a
[GitHub App](#github-app-authentication) installation. Either needs at minimum the following
read-only permissions:

- Actions (read-only) - Used to pull workflow jobs and success
- Administration (read-only) - Used to check configuration and rulesets for a repository
- Contents (read-only) - Used to read repository files such as `go.mod` when dependency health collection is enabled
- Metadata (read-only) - Required by GitHub
- Pull Requests (read-only) - Used to pull PRs and status
- Secret scanning alerts (read-only) - Used to check if secrets have been found
- Secret scanning push protection bypass requests (read-only) - Used to check the process of any bypass requests

When dependency health collection is enabled, the token also uses repository contents, Actions, pull requests, license, and dependency graph/SBOM APIs against resolved public GitHub dependency repositories. Missing permissions or unavailable upstream data for resolved dependency repositories are recorded as dependency-level collection gaps and do not fail the repository evaluation.

## Configuration

```yaml
plugins:
  github_repos:
    token: "gh-pat-abc123"
    # Or authenticate as a GitHub App instead of setting token (see below):
    # app_id: "123456"
    # installation_id: "78901234"
    # private_key_file: /etc/ccf/github-app.pem
    # Organization which you want to check the repos of
    organization: octocat
    # The following items are mutually exclusive, so cannot be set together. If neither are set, all repos are
    # pulled and tested, otherwise the selection is chosen below
    # Alternatively, these can be limited via the PAT configuration
    included_repositories: foo,bar,baz
    excluded_repositories: quix,quiz
    # Optional dependency health collection. Disabled by default to avoid extra GitHub API usage.
    dependency_health_enabled: "false"
    dependency_health_max_dependencies: "50"
    dependency_health_closed_pr_lookback_days: "180"
    dependency_health_include_unresolved: "true"
    dependency_health_collect_sbom: "true"
    dependency_health_pr_interaction_sample_size: "20"
```

Dependency health collection currently parses direct `go.mod` dependencies only. It resolves module paths that start with `github.com/{owner}/{repo}` and collects public upstream repository health signals.
Dependency policies are now evaluated using policy behavior metadata from the request (`dependency` behavior), and dependency inputs expose repository/dependency context under `input.dependency` and `input.repository` with request policy data available at `input.policy_data`. This can add several GitHub API calls per direct dependency, so enable it only for policy collections that need dependency evidence.

Policy input migration: use request `policy_data` for new policy-specific inputs. The legacy plugin config key `policy_input` is still accepted as a JSON string fallback when request `policy_data` is not provided, and repository policy evaluation exposes the same data under both `input.policy_data` and the legacy `input.policy_input` key for compatibility. If both `policy_data` and `policy_input` are provided, `policy_data` is used.


### GitHub App authentication

Instead of a token, the plugin can authenticate as a GitHub App installed on the organization.
Organizations can govern apps centrally, and the plugin only ever holds short-lived
installation tokens, which it renews as they expire.

1. Create a GitHub App (organization *Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps*) with the
   read-only repository permissions listed above, and generate a private key for it.
2. Install the app on the organization, for all repositories or the ones the plugin checks.
3. Configure the plugin with the app's ID, the installation's ID (the number at the end of the
   installation's settings URL) and the private key:

```yaml
plugins:
  github_repos:
    app_id: "123456"
    installation_id: "78901234"
    # The PEM file the app's "Generate a private key" downloads (preferred), or
    private_key_file: /etc/ccf/github-app.pem
    # the key inline, as PEM or base64-encoded PEM (e.g. from an environment variable)
    # private_key: "LS0tLS1CRUdJTi..."
    organization: octocat
```

A `token`, when set, takes precedence over the app settings.

## Policy input

The plugin evaluates two kinds of input, and a policy bundle gets one of them. A repository policy receives one document per repository as `input`. A dependency policy receives one document per direct dependency of a repository. Bundles are matched by the behavior the agent assigns them: `dependency` for the bundle `plugin-github-repositories-dependency-policies`, `repository` for every other bundle. Dependency documents are only produced when `dependency_health_enabled` is on. The table lists fields by their path inside the document. Many repository fields are GitHub REST API objects, passed through as GitHub returns them, so only their top level is described here. A field marked as left out is missing from the document, not null. Any other field is always present, but a list or an object the plugin found nothing for can be `null`, so test for that. Your own policy data from the agent configuration is in `input.policy_data` on both kinds of document. Older agent configurations set it with the `policy_input` setting; the repository document still carries the same data a second time under the legacy key `input.policy_input`, which the dependency document does not have.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `settings` | object | Repository document. The repository as the GitHub REST API returns it (name, full_name, owner, default_branch, visibility, archived, security_and_analysis and the rest). |
| `workflows` | array of objects | Repository document. GitHub Actions workflows configured in the repository (id, name, path, state). |
| `workflow_runs` | array of objects | Repository document. Workflow runs the plugin collected, as GitHub returns them. |
| `protected_branches` | array of strings | Repository document. Names of the protected branches. |
| `branch_protection_rules` | object (branch name to object) | Repository document. The full branch protection configuration of each branch, as GitHub returns it. A branch whose protection could not be read is missing. When no protected branch was read, the default branch is tried. |
| `required_status_checks` | object (branch name to object) | Repository document. The required status checks of each branch that has them. |
| `sbom` | object | Repository document. The repository's SBOM from the dependency graph, as GitHub returns it. `null` when none is available. |
| `last_release` | object | Repository document. The latest release, as GitHub returns it. `null` when the repository has no release. |
| `pull_requests` | array of objects | Repository document. Open pull requests, each with every field GitHub returns for a pull request plus `reviews`. |
| `pull_requests[].reviews` | array of objects | Reviews of the pull request, each with every field GitHub returns for a review plus `threads`. |
| `pull_requests[].reviews[].threads` | array of objects | Discussion threads of the review. |
| `pull_requests[].reviews[].threads[].id` | string | Thread ID. |
| `pull_requests[].reviews[].threads[].is_resolved` | boolean | Whether the thread is resolved. |
| `pull_requests[].reviews[].threads[].comments` | array of objects | Comments in the thread. Each has `id`, `body`, `url`, `diff_hunk` and `path`, and may have `review_id`, `position`, `original_position`, `reply_to_id`, `created_at` and `updated_at`, which are left out when empty. |
| `code_owners` | object | Repository document. The CODEOWNERS file as GitHub returns repository content. `null` when the repository has none. |
| `org_teams` | array of objects | Repository document. Teams of the organization: `id` (integer), `name`, `slug` and `members` (array of logins). |
| `deployments` | array of objects | Repository document. Deployments that match the plugin's deployment settings. Each has `deployment` (the GitHub deployment) and `statuses` (its GitHub deployment statuses). |
| `failed_deployments` | array of objects | Repository document. Every deployment that has a failed status, in the same shape as `deployments`. |
| `collaborators` | array of objects | Repository document. Direct collaborators: `login`, `role_name` and `permissions` (object, permission name to boolean). |
| `repository_teams` | array of objects | Repository document. Teams with access to the repository: `id` (integer), `name`, `slug`, `permission`, `permissions` (object, permission name to boolean) and `members` (array of logins). |
| `environments` | array of objects | Repository document. Deployment environments. Each has `id`, `name`, `can_admins_bypass`, and may have `url`, `html_url`, `wait_timer`, `reviewers`, `protection_rules` and `deployment_branch_policy`, which are left out when empty. |
| `environments[].reviewers` | array of objects | Required reviewers: `type`, and as they apply `id`, `login`, `slug` and `name`, left out when empty. |
| `environments[].protection_rules` | array of objects | Protection rules: `id`, `type`, `prevent_self_review`, and `wait_timer` and `reviewers` when set. |
| `environments[].deployment_branch_policy` | object | `protected_branches` and `custom_branch_policies`, both boolean. |
| `effective_branch_rules` | object (branch name to object) | Repository document. The rules that apply to each branch, from branch protection and rulesets together. Each object has `required_signatures` (boolean), and may have `required_deployments` (array of environment names), `code_scanning_tools` (array of strings), `required_approving_review_count` (integer), `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push` and `require_code_owner_review` (booleans). These are left out when empty, 0 or false. |
| `policy_data` | object | Both documents. The policy data from the agent configuration. An empty object when none is set. |
| `policy_input` | object | Repository document only. Legacy key, the same data as `policy_data`. Use `policy_data`. |
| `repository` | object | Dependency document. The repository that declares the dependency. |
| `repository.organization` | string | Organization login. |
| `repository.name` | string | Repository name. |
| `repository.full_name` | string | `organization/name`. |
| `repository.url` | string | Web URL of the repository. Left out when empty. |
| `dependency` | object | Dependency document. One direct dependency. Today only direct `go.mod` dependencies are read. |
| `dependency.name` | string | Module path. |
| `dependency.ecosystem` | string | Package ecosystem. |
| `dependency.source_file` | string | File the dependency was declared in. |
| `dependency.direct` | boolean | Whether the dependency is direct. |
| `dependency.declared_version` | string | Version declared in the source file. |
| `dependency.repository` | object | The upstream repository the dependency resolves to. `provider`, `owner`, `name` and `url` are left out when empty. |
| `dependency.repository.resolved` | boolean | Whether the module path was resolved to a public GitHub repository. |
| `dependency.health` | object | Maintenance signals of the upstream repository. `null` when not collected. |
| `dependency.health.repository_archived` | boolean | Whether the upstream repository is archived. |
| `dependency.health.latest_release` | object | `tag` and `published_at` (RFC 3339 time) of the latest release. Left out when there is none. |
| `dependency.health.latest_commit` | object | `sha` and `committed_at` (RFC 3339 time) of the latest default-branch commit. Left out when unknown. |
| `dependency.health.workflows` | object | `count` (integer) of workflows, and `latest_default_branch_run` with `status`, `conclusion` and `created_at` when a run exists. Left out when not collected. |
| `dependency.health.pull_requests` | object | Pull request activity. `open_count`, `open_count_capped`, `recent_closed_count`, `recent_closed_count_capped` and `first_interaction_sampled_pull_requests` are always there; `oldest_open_created_at`, `median_days_to_close` and `median_hours_to_first_interaction` are left out when unknown. Left out as a whole when not collected. |
| `dependency.supply_chain` | object | License and SBOM facts. `null` when not collected. |
| `dependency.supply_chain.license` | object | `collected` (boolean), and `spdx_id`, `name` and `url` when known. |
| `dependency.supply_chain.sbom` | object | `available` (boolean), `package_count` (integer), `collected` (boolean), and `spdx_id`, `spdx_version` and `creation_info_created` when known. |
| `dependency.collection_status` | object | Which collection stages finished: `dependency_parsed`, `repository_resolved`, `health_collected`, `license_collected` and `sbom_collected`, all boolean. A missing upstream fact is recorded here and does not fail the run. |
| `dependency.collection_status.errors` | array of objects | Non-fatal collection failures, each with `scope` and `message` strings. |

An example input:

```json
{
  "repository": {
    "organization": "example-org",
    "name": "payments-api",
```

## Subject templates

The subject templates this plugin registers. Each example is built from sample data.

### github-repository

A GitHub repository. Title: `GitHub Repository: {{ .repository }}`. Dependency evaluations use the labels `type` (`repository-dependency`), `dependency`, `ecosystem` and `dependency_version` on top of these, and repository evaluations use `provider` (`github`) and `type` (`repository`); none of those are part of the identity.

| Identity key | Description |
|---|---|
| `repository` | Name of the repository, without the organization. |
| `organization` | Login of the GitHub organization that owns the repository. |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "github-repository",
  "type": "component",
  "title": "GitHub Repository: payments-api",
  "description": "GitHub repository payments-api in organization example-org",
  "purpose": "Represents a GitHub repository being monitored for compliance",
  "identityLabels": {
    "repository": "payments-api",
    "organization": "example-org"
  }
}
```

## Policies

The policy bundles that work with this plugin, at their newest releases. The controls are the ones the bundle's policies list in their metadata.

| Bundle | Latest version | Controls covered | Compatible plugin lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`plugin-github-repositories-custom-policies`](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-github-repositories-custom-policies) | `v0.2.1` | *none listed* | latest |
| [`plugin-github-repositories-dependency-policies`](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-github-repositories-dependency-policies) | `v0.1.2` | *none listed* | latest |
| [`plugin-github-repositories-policies`](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-github-repositories-policies) | `v0.7.4` | *none listed* | latest |
| [`plugin-github-repositories-pr-policies`](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-github-repositories-pr-policies) | `v0.2.1` | *none listed* | latest |

When writing OPA/Rego policies for this plugin, they must be added under the `compliance_framework` Rego package:

```rego
# deny_critical_severity.rego
# package compliance_framework.[YOUR_RULE_PATH]
package compliance_framework.deny_critical_severity
```
